RS was carried out by argon gas atomizing the alloy melt and subsequent splat quenching onto a water-cooled copper roll. The cooling rate during rapid solidification was estimated to be about 5×10^5 K s-1
The flakes were consolidated to the P/M materials by cold pressing, vacuum degassing and hot extrusion.
Vacuum degassing was done in 1.33×10-3 Pa at 573 K for 7.2 ks.
Hot extrusion was carried out at 673 K with a reduction ratio of 25:1. Finally, extruded round bars of 7 mm in diameter were obtained as the P/M materials.
RS was carried out by argon gas atomizing the alloy melt and subsequent splat quenching onto a water-cooled copper roll.
I/M materials were prepared from homogenized alloy ingots under the same extrusion conditions as the reference material.
tensile properties of P/M materials annealed at 773 K for 18 ks were obtained at the same initial strain rates.
Uniform dispersion of fine intermetallic compounds (Co2Al9) was observed in all the as-extruded P/M materials.
Coarse rod shaped Co compounds of which length is 20-30 µm are observed in the I/M counterparts.
Hardness of Al-5Co-5Mg alloy is highest (142HV) for the P/M material whereas it is not so for the I/M material.
Both dispersion strengthening of fine Co compounds and solid solution hardening of Mg contribute to a substantial increase in hardness and tensile strength in the RS-P/M materials of Al-Co-Mg alloys.

The easiness for diffusion of solute Mg atom in the matrix is thought as a cause of decreasing tensile strength and creep strength of the P/M materials at higher temperature.
Al-2mass%Co and Al-5mass%Co alloys with varied Mg additions of 0, 1 and 5 mass% were prepared by rapid solidification techniques.

It was roughly estimated that dispersion strengthening of Co compounds in RS-P/M materials was suppressed by solute Mg at high temperature due to the easiness for diffusion of solute Mg in the aluminum matrix.
